content.text:
I submitted index 20 (Sb fraction 0.624). It had the highest EQE of the five compositions I measured: 0.0559%.

All five EQE measurements are used. I didn't use any of the five XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present is unconfirmed.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.361 | 0.0173 |
| 12 | 0.503 | 0.0116 |
| **20** | **0.624** | **0.0559** |
| 22 | 0.671 | 0.0463 |
| 28 | 0.710 | 0.0250 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is low on the Pb-rich side, highest between Sb 0.62 and 0.67, and drops again at 0.71. The best region sits near the composition of the known phase PbSb₂O₆ (Sb 0.667).
- **Light absorption:** The band-gap model predicts about 2.7 eV for PbSb₂O₆ and 2.5 eV for Pb₂Sb₂O₇. Both are below the 3.2 eV illumination, so both should absorb it. That alone doesn't explain why the Sb-rich films perform better.
- **What could be missed:** Five points can't pin down the peak. Compositions between Sb 0.57 and 0.62 (indices 18–19) and between 0.62 and 0.67 (index 21) were never measured, and one of them could beat index 20.
